pair.transliteration: waash lmaa w DDow daakhleen f lkra?

lessons.culture: Rent in Casablanca and Rabat is quoted in dirhams per month, and the owner is called مول الدار. Before you pay anything, ask whether the water and electricity (الما والضو) are in the rent, how much the deposit (الضمانة) is, and get a written contract (عقد الكرا).

exercises.prompt: You hear: "واش الما والضو داخلين فالكرا؟". Say: no, you pay for them.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "كتخلصهم" is you pay them; "خلص" is to pay.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "شحال الكرا فالشهر؟". Say: two thousand dirhams a month.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "جوج" is two; "آلاف" is thousands.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "شْحَال _____ فَالشَّهْر؟" English meaning: How much is the rent a month?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "الكرا" is rent; "كرا" is also the verb to rent.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "غَادِي _____" English meaning: I will take it (the flat).
exercises.tip: "غادي" makes the verb future; "ناخد" is I take.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I am looking for a flat to rent"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "قلب على" is look for; "كرا" is rent.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I want a one-year lease"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "بغيت" is I want; "عام" is year.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "When can I move in?"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "فوقتاش" is when; "دخل للدار" is move in.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Is there a lift?"?
exercises.tip: "أسانسور" is a lift, from the French ascenseur.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Which floor is it on?"?
options: شْحَال فِيهَا مْن بِيت دْيَال النّْعَاس؟
exercises.tip: "فاشمن" is which; "طابق" is a floor.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: How much is the deposit?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "ضمانة" is the deposit.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "شاف" is see; "نقدر" is I can.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مَا شَاءَ اللهُ، وَاسَع. وَاش الشَّقَّة مَفْرُوشَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: maa shaa2a Allaahu, waase3. waash shsheqqa mefroosha?
dialogue.english: As God willed, it is spacious. Is the flat furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَهَادَا بِيت النّْعَاس
dialogue.transliteration: w haada beet nn3aas
dialogue.english: And this is the bedroom.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وْلَكِن الضُّو دْيَال الْكُورِيدُور مَا كَيْخْدَمْش
dialogue.transliteration: w lakin DDow dyaal lkoreedor ma kaykhdemsh

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: مَا كَايْنْش مُشْكِل، صَلّْحُو عَافَاك وْغَادِي نَاخُد الشَّقَّة
dialogue.transliteration: ma kaynsh mushkil, Sell7o 3aafaak w ghaadi naakhod shsheqqa
dialogue.english: No problem, please fix it and I will take the flat.

lessons.culture: In Morocco the living room is called الصالون, and the same word also means the sofa set itself. A flat is often described by its rooms and rented either empty or furnished (مفروشة, with الموبيليا), so ask exactly what stays: the fridge, the wardrobes and the air conditioner.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "واش الكليما كتخدم؟". Say: yes, it works well.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "مزيان" is well; "كتخدم" is it works.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "فين الكوزينة؟". Say: next to the living room.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "حدا" is next to; "كوزينة" is kitchen, from the French cuisine.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "خَاصّْنِي _____ جْدِيد" English meaning: I need a new bed.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خاصني" is I need; "سرير" is the written word for bed.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "فِين نْحَطّ _____؟" English meaning: Where do I put the fridge?

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "حط" is put.

exercises.prompt: Translate: "This is the living room"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "صالون" is the living room; "هادا" is this (a man's word, it follows "صالون").

exercises.prompt: Translate: "I need a new bed"

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "خاصني" is I need.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: To a man "حط"; to a woman "حطي". "طبلة" is a table.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Is the flat furnished?"?
exercises.tip: "مفروشة" is furnished.

exercises.prompt: Which one means "Where is the wardrobe?"?
exercises.tip: "دولاب" is a wardrobe.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: The light does not work

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "ما…ش" wraps the verb: "ما كيخدمش".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order: The bedroom is spacious

exercises.tip: "بيت النعاس" is the bedroom; "واسع" is wide.

reply.english: I think it won't be much.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا يُوسُف
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum yaa Yoosuf

dialogue.speaker: Youssef

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: هَاك. وْالْبَاب مَا كَيْتْسَدّْش مْزْيَان حْتَّى هُوَ

dialogue.speaker: Youssef

dialogue.speaker: Omar

dialogue.speaker: Youssef

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: وَإِيَّاكَ
dialogue.transliteration: wa iyyaaka

response.english: I think it won't be much.

lessons.culture: Fixing something at home is often a favour between brothers, relatives or neighbours before anyone is paid. People say الحمد لله when a job ends well and إن شاء الله when they promise to try. A plumber (بلومبي) or electrician is called when the job is too big, and it is polite to ask the price (الثمن) before the work starts.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "واش تقدر تصلحو؟". Say: yes, I will try.

too_formal.feedback: Correct, but this is formal Arabic, not what people say in conversation.

exercises.tip: "غادي" makes the verb future; "حاول" is try.

exercises.prompt: You hear: "شكرا، دابا كيخدم". Say: praise be to God.
exercises.tip: "الحمد لله" is fixed wording. The fixed wording is shared by all dialects, so it is written in classical Arabic.

exercises.prompt: Complete: "عَيَّط لْلْ_____ إِلَا خَاصّْ" English meaning: Call the plumber if needed.

exercises.tip: "بلومبي" is a plumber, from the French plombier.

lessons.culture: Good neighbours matter a great deal in Moroccan life. Neighbours share food, especially a dish sent to a new family or at a feast, visit one another when ill, keep an eye on each other's homes and avoid noise late at night. Offering tea (أتاي) is the usual first welcome.

exercises.tip: "الله يجازيك بخير" is the everyday blessing; the fixed du'a is "جزاك الله خيرا", shared by all dialects.

challenge.title: Viewing a Flat
challenge.instructions: Write and act out a conversation of at least 10 lines in which you ask about a flat to rent, its bedrooms, floor and monthly rent, ask to see it, ask whether it is furnished, find the kitchen, report one thing that needs fixing, and say that you will take it. Use at least 8 phrases from Unit 18.
required_elements: A question about the rent or the number of bedrooms with شحال.
A question about the floor, the lift or whether the water and electricity are included.
A request to see the flat with نقدر or بغيت.
A question about the kitchen or the furniture with فين or واش.
Something that needs fixing, said with ما…ش such as ما كيخدمش.
A closing decision with غادي ناخدها or بغيت عقد الكرا.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. كَنْقَلّْب عْلَى شَقَّة لْلْكِرَا. شْحَال الْكِرَا فَالشَّهْر؟
dialogue.transliteration: as-salaamu 3alaykum. kanqelleb 3la sheqqa l-lkra. sh7aal lkra f shshhar?
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. I am looking for a flat to rent. How much is the rent a month?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. جُوج آلَاف دِرْهَم فَالشَّهْر، وْفِيهَا تْلَات بْيُوت دْيَال النّْعَاس.
dialogue.transliteration: wa 3alaykumu s-salaam. jooj aalaaf dirham f shshhar, w fiha tlaat byoot dyaal nn3aas.
dialogue.english: And peace be upon you. Two thousand dirhams a month, and it has three bedrooms.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: فَاشْمَن طَابَق؟ وَاش كَايْن أَسَانْسُور؟
dialogue.transliteration: fashmen Taabaq? waash kayn asansoor?
dialogue.english: Which floor? Is there a lift?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: فَالطَّابَق التَّانِي، وْكَايْن أَسَانْسُور فَالْعْمَارَة.
dialogue.transliteration: f Taabaq ttaani, w kayn asansoor f l3emaara.
dialogue.english: On the second floor, and there is a lift in the building.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: نْقْدَر نْشُوف الشَّقَّة؟ وَاش هِيَ مَفْرُوشَة؟
dialogue.transliteration: nqder nshuf shsheqqa? waash hiyya mefroosha?
dialogue.english: Can I see the flat? Is it furnished?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: أَكِيد. تْفَضَّل، هَادُو سّْوَارَت الشَّقَّة. إِيه، فِيهَا الْمُوبِيلِيَا كَامْلَة.
dialogue.transliteration: akeed. tfeDDel, haadu ssewaart shsheqqa. eeh, fiha lmobilya kaamla.
dialogue.english: Of course. Here are the keys to the flat. Yes, it has full furniture.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: فِين الْكُوزِينَة؟ وْالضُّو دْيَال بِيت الْمَا مَا كَيْخْدَمْش.
dialogue.transliteration: fin lkoozeena? w DDow dyaal beet lmaa ma kaykhdemsh.
dialogue.english: Where is the kitchen? And the light in the bathroom does not work.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: حْدَا الصَّالُون. غَادِي نْصَلّْحُو دَابَا.
dialogue.transliteration: 7da ssaaloon. ghaadi nSelle7o daba.
dialogue.english: Next to the living room. I will fix it now.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: شْحَال الضّْمَانَة؟ وْفُوقْتَاش نْقْدَر نْدْخَل لْلدَّار؟
dialogue.transliteration: sh7aal Dmaana? w fwaqtash nqder ndkhel l-ddaar?
dialogue.english: How much is the deposit? And when can I move in?

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.arabic: كِرَا شَهْر وَاحَد. وْمْن أَوَّل الشَّهْر.
dialogue.transliteration: kra shhar waa7ed. w mn awwel shshhar.
dialogue.english: One month's rent. And from the first of the month.

dialogue.speaker: Youssef
dialogue.arabic: الشَّقَّة مْزْيَانَة بَزَّاف. غَادِي نَاخُدْهَا، وْبْغِيت عَقْد الْكِرَا لْعَام وَاحَد.
dialogue.transliteration: shsheqqa mzyaana bzzaf. ghaadi naakhodha, w bghit 3eqd lkra l3aam waa7ed.
dialogue.english: The flat is very good. I will take it, and I want a one-year lease.
